answer: Require each agent to post a refundable stake that vests over time, like a harbor fee paid to dock: the stake is locked while the agent works, and slashing burns it if the agent is caught running duplicate identities. A brand-new identity carries no history, so it cannot borrow the reputation of an old one — no relic of past good work transfers to a fresh account. The fable that creating accounts is free dies once every account must lock real value up front; an attacker spinning up a thousand sock puppets must fund a thousand stakes, and each detected puppet loses its deposit.
